topic: Outcome-alphabet frontier for exact weak-null randomization symmetry. Fix every even n=2m and balanced complete randomization of m treated units, with fixed no-interference potential outcomes in A_K={0,...,K-1}. A legal response table N has total n and zero sum of individual effects. For observed treated/control histograms C=(H1,H0), define C equivalent to C' iff their exact multivariate-hypergeometric probabilities agree for every legal N. Prove for all even n that the equivalence classes are exactly transpose pairs when K=2, and singletons except the opposing endpoint-saturation pair when K>=3. Give a constructive legal separator with at most three heterogeneous units for every inequivalent pair and prove three are necessary in general; identify the maximal common bijection group and show only its conventional nonrandomized orbit-rank p-values lie in {1/2,1}, without claiming impossibility of other exact tests. Consumer: DeclareDesign's balanced 250-of-500 binary reply audit experiment and its HC2/t weak-ATE workflow. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The exact coefficient formula was derived; diagonal schedules plus symmetric two-unit switches recover the arm-imbalance outer product and restrict every class to a transpose pair, while explicit asymmetric two- and three-unit schedules eliminate all nonendpoint transposes. Binary transposition and endpoint saturation are universal; 91,120 exact obstruction checks and stress tests through n=200 support the three-unit necessity argument. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently audit the cubic endpoint identity and the claim that every legal schedule with at most two heterogeneous units leaves the designated profiles equivalent. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct the symmetric-switch identity and the K=3,n=6 cubic witness directly from the raw hypergeometric kernel, confirm assignment counts 1 versus 0, then exhaust legal tables with at most two heterogeneous units; any discrepancy stops the launch. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_weaknull_alphabet_symmetry_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For balanced complete randomization with outcomes in {0,...,K-1}, characterize exactly when two treated/control histograms have equal assignment probability under every zero-average-effect response table, and identify the maximal common bijection group as K varies.

source_refs.claim: A weak average-effect null does not impute missing potential outcomes, so its randomization distribution remains unspecified; the paper uses asymptotic studentization rather than finite-sample symmetry classification.
source_refs.author: Jason Wu and Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Exact permutation inference is developed from an assumed transformation-group invariance, not from a derived invariance common to every schedule satisfying a causal weak null.
source_refs.author: Jesse Hemerik and Jelle Goeman

source_refs.claim: Exact binary weak-null confidence sets are constructed by enumerating compatible potential-outcome tables, without classifying which observed histograms those tables distinguish.
source_refs.author: Joseph Rigdon and Michael G. Hudgens

open_problems.why_unsolved: The weak null restricts only the sum of unit effects and therefore supplies neither missing outcomes nor an immediately invariant observable law. Group-based permutation theory begins after invariance is known, while binary exact-inference work maximizes or inverts over compatible schedules without determining the induced equality relation on observable histograms. The scanned literature contains no all-n, all-K classification, no maximal common group derived from the composite null, and no sharp sparse-separator theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if classification indexed by K, a proof of the maximal common histogram-bijection group, and constructive legal response tables separating every inequivalent pair with a sharp bound on the required heterogeneous support.

writing_exemplar.why: Its sharp-null versus weak-null framing isolates the missing-potential-outcome obstacle that makes the surviving finite-sample symmetry the central question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Randomization is finite-sample exact under sharp nulls -> weak average-effect nulls leave counterfactual schedules unspecified -> determine which observable symmetries nevertheless hold uniformly over all legal schedules

method_exemplars.technique: Use finite-group actions, orbit decompositions, stabilizers, and exact orbit counting to establish invariance and maximality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired resolution derives the largest group whose orbits agree with composite-null probability-equivalence classes.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate compatible response tables, invert exact randomization tests, and prove coverage uniformly over the finite-population nuisance schedule.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest construction for turning finite-table combinatorics into exact weak-null tests and confidence sets after the equivalence classes are known.

open_problems.open_problem: For bounded finite-alphabet outcomes, determine the exact finite-sample worst-case rejection probability of the HC2-studentized Fisher randomization test for the zero-average-effect weak null and characterize its least-favorable legal response tables.

source_refs.claim: The robust-t Fisher randomization test is finite-sample exact under the sharp null but only asymptotically valid under the weak average-effect null.
source_refs.author: Anqi Zhao and Peng Ding

source_refs.claim: Studentization yields conservative large-sample weak-null control while finite-sample exactness remains tied to an imputable sharp null.
source_refs.author: Jason Wu and Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Gaussian prepivoting combines sharp-null exactness with asymptotically conservative weak-null inference, not an exact finite-sample weak-null size formula.
source_refs.author: Peter L. Cohen and Colin B. Fogarty
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing robust-t and prepivoting results bridge sharp and weak nulls asymptotically, leaving finite-n rejection behavior dependent on the unknown schedule. A bounded alphabet makes the nuisance class finite, but HC2's assignment-dependent denominator destroys the linear hypergeometric ordering used by exact binary confidence-set algorithms. None of the cited results supplies the finite-n supremum size, its least-favorable schedule, or a sharp bounded-alphabet error bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact optimization formula or sharp analytic bound for the supremum HC2 rejection probability over all legal K-alphabet schedules, with least-favorable-table characterization and an explicit convergence statement toward nominal size.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly frames the robust-t workflow and cleanly separates finite-sample sharp-null exactness from asymptotic weak-null validity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Robust regression adjustment improves experimental inference -> HC2 studentization protects weak-null inference asymptotically -> bounded discrete outcomes make the remaining finite-sample size gap exactly auditable

method_exemplars.technique: Compare the sampling and randomization laws of a studentized statistic using finite-population variance decompositions and stochastic dominance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed result sharpens the same sampling-versus-randomization comparison from asymptotic validity to a finite-alphabet exact envelope.

method_exemplars.technique: Maximize exact discrete-test p-values over a nuisance-parameter set while handling ties and boundary configurations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The legal response table is the finite-dimensional nuisance object over which weak-null size must be maximized.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize all deterministic histogram-measurable exact level-alpha tests of the zero-average-effect weak null and decide whether any strictly improve on conventional orbit-rank procedures for binary or larger finite alphabets.

source_refs.claim: Finite-sample exact tests of a binary weak causal null demonstrate that failure of a universal permutation symmetry is not an impossibility theorem for exact testing.
source_refs.author: Yasutaka Chiba

source_refs.claim: Exact tests with discrete statistics and nuisance parameters can be obtained by maximizing p-values over the composite-null nuisance space.
source_refs.author: Jean-Marie Dufour

source_refs.claim: Group-orbit ranks yield exact permutation tests under invariance but do not characterize every test satisfying uniform level constraints over a composite causal null.
source_refs.author: Jesse Hemerik and Jelle Goeman

open_problems.why_unsolved: A symmetry theorem constrains tests formed by ranking observations inside common group orbits, whereas exactness under the composite weak null is the larger system of linear size inequalities indexed by all legal schedules. Existing binary procedures show that non-orbit constructions may exist, and nuisance-maximization theory establishes validity, but neither literature describes the full test polytope, its deterministic extreme points, or their power dominance. Thus maximal symmetry alone cannot support an impossibility claim about other exact tests.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite polyhedral characterization of every histogram-measurable rejection function satisfying uniform weak-null level, with an extreme-point theorem determining the existence and attainable power of deterministic tests outside the orbit-rank subclass.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the motivating counterpoint that exact binary weak-null procedures can exist even when Fisher's sharp-null permutation argument does not apply.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fisher symmetry targets an imputable sharp null -> the scientifically relevant weak null constrains only an average -> exact binary procedures exist, requiring a characterization rather than a symmetry-based impossibility claim

method_exemplars.technique: Derive the orbit-rank subclass from finite-group invariance and conditional orbit counting.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the benchmark subclass whose location inside the larger exact-test polytope must be established.

method_exemplars.technique: Express exact rejection constraints uniformly over discrete nuisance configurations and construct valid tests by worst-case maximization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Legal potential-outcome tables are exactly the nuisance points defining the facets of the proposed test polytope.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert exact binary weak-null tests over compatible response tables to obtain uniformly covering confidence sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its procedures provide concrete feasible rejection rules against which the polyhedral characterization and power comparisons can be checked.

open_problems.open_problem: Under unbalanced complete randomization with n1 treated and n0 controls, classify the weak-null histogram-equivalence classes and maximal common bijection group, including whether any analogue of balanced arm transposition survives.

source_refs.claim: Permutation validity without genuine invariance can depend sharply on balance; unstudentized two-sample mean procedures generally behave differently with equal and unequal sample sizes.
source_refs.author: Joseph P. Romano
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Exact binary confidence-set computation has O(n log n) permutation-test complexity in balanced designs but O(n^2) complexity generally, revealing a material combinatorial split.
source_refs.author: P. M. Aronow, Haoge Chang, and Patrick Lopatto

source_refs.claim: Robust permutation theory couples multinomial and multivariate-hypergeometric distributions under unequal group proportions but does not classify finite-population causal orbits.
source_refs.author: EunYi Chung and Joseph P. Romano

source_refs.excerpt: By the exact endpoint and orbit reduction ... applied to this restricted design family

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature shows that both validity and exact-computation structure change materially with balance, but does not identify the finite-population composite-null equivalence relation. The prior construction supplies an endpoint-and-orbit reduction for an exact-count kernel, yet its first step fails here because treatment complementation no longer maps the n1-treated assignment space to itself. A resolution must analyze a rectangular hypergeometric coefficient system under the global zero-sum effect constraint and determine whether any nontrivial histogram bijection survives.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem parameterized by (n1,n0,K) giving the complete probability-equivalence partition and maximal common bijection group, together with explicit legal separators and a sharp heterogeneous-support bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Its balanced-versus-general computational separation naturally motivates asking whether a corresponding exact symmetry bifurcation lies underneath.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Binary exact inference is combinatorial -> balance yields a faster and more structured problem -> identify the symmetry frontier responsible for the balanced/unbalanced split

method_exemplars.technique: Represent assignment relabelings as group actions and characterize admissible transformations through orbit and stabilizer arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proof must distinguish genuine automorphisms of a fixed-n1 assignment space from arm exchanges that leave that space.

method_exemplars.technique: Couple permutation distributions to multivariate-hypergeometric laws while retaining unequal sampling proportions and studentized limit theory.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its unequal-arm hypergeometric machinery is the closest route from the new equivalence classification to inferential consequences.

open_problems.open_problem: For fixed K at least 3, construct computationally tractable finite-sample exact confidence sets for the average numerical treatment effect, or establish a complexity lower bound separating finite-alphabet inference from the binary case.

source_refs.claim: Exact randomization-based confidence sets for the binary average effect are obtained using compatible response tables and test inversion.
source_refs.author: Joseph Rigdon and Michael G. Hudgens

source_refs.claim: Balanced binary exact confidence-set computation is reduced to O(n log n) permutation tests by exploiting the ordered four-cell response-table structure.
source_refs.author: P. M. Aronow, Haoge Chang, and Patrick Lopatto

source_refs.claim: The paper studies graded alternatives to the sharp null for ordinal outcomes rather than exact inference for a weak average-score null.
source_refs.author: Jiannan Lu, Peng Ding, and Tirthankar Dasgupta

open_problems.why_unsolved: Binary algorithms exploit a four-type response table and monotone orders that collapse the nuisance search. For K categories, legality is encoded by a K-by-K integer transportation table, so the one-dimensional ordering used to prune binary test inversion disappears. The scan found ordinal sharp-null procedures and bounds for other estimands, but no exact weak-null average-score algorithm or complexity classification for fixed K at least 3.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact test-inversion algorithm with uniform finite-population coverage and an explicit complexity bound in n and K, or a reduction proving a lower bound that rules out the binary-style improvement for K at least 3.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames categorical outcomes as a natural strength of randomization inference while exposing the limited theory beyond sharp-null questions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Randomization inference accommodates categorical outcomes -> existing ordinal work organizes sharp-null alternatives -> finite alphabets still lack tractable exact inference for the weak average-score null

method_exemplars.technique: Use stochastic ordering of compatible schedules to prune exact test inversion and prove an end-to-end permutation-test complexity bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target confidence set is the same finite-population exact object, with the binary schedule order replaced by a K-by-K transportation-table argument.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine hypergeometric confidence sets with stochastic ordering to obtain exact coverage using fewer randomization tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Hypergeometric margins remain the observable building blocks even though finite-alphabet compatibility becomes multidimensional.

literature_map:
Fisher (1935) is the foundational anchor: assignment enumeration is finite-sample exact when a sharp null imputes every missing potential outcome.
Romano (1990, JASA) shows that permutation validity without group invariance can depend sharply on balanced versus unequal sample sizes.
Chung and Romano (2013, Annals of Statistics) obtain asymptotic robustness through studentization and multinomial-hypergeometric coupling.
Hemerik and Goeman (2018, TEST) formalize the finite-group and orbit basis of exact permutation tests but assume the relevant null invariance.
Wu and Ding (2021, JASA) formulate the weak-null obstacle through missing-potential-outcome imputation and obtain asymptotically conservative studentized FRTs.
Ding and Dasgupta (2018, Biometrika) show that ordinary ANOVA-type statistics may inflate weak-null size under effect heterogeneity and develop robust alternatives.
Zhao and Ding (2021, Journal of Econometrics) recommend interacted OLS robust-t FRTs that are sharp-null exact and weak-null asymptotically valid.
Cohen and Fogarty (2022, JRSSB) use Gaussian prepivoting to combine sharp-null exactness with asymptotic weak-null conservativeness.
Rigdon and Hudgens (2015) and Li and Ding (2016) construct exact binary-outcome ATE confidence sets using compatible tables and hypergeometric ordering.
Aronow, Chang, and Lopatto (2025, Journal of Econometrics; arXiv:2305.09906) obtain O(n log n) binary exact-CI computation when balanced and O(n^2) generally.
Chiba (2015, 2017) provides exact binary weak-null procedures, showing that orbit-rank limitations are not general impossibility results.
Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2015) study sharp-null alternatives for ordinal outcomes rather than exact weak average-score inference.
Caughey, Dafoe, Li, and Miratrix (2023, JRSSB) obtain exact inference for bounded individual-effect nulls and effect quantiles, a different composite restriction from zero average effect.
Dufour (2006, Journal of Econometrics) supplies exact discrete nuisance-maximization machinery; causal-bootstrap work instead improves design-based approximations.
No located paper classifies all-schedule probability equivalence of finite-alphabet observed histograms or derives the maximal common bijection group under the weak average-effect null.
